To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a set of national data elements for the management of patients with an acute coronary syndrome that are consistent with international standards and can be used to facilitate quality improvement, research and clinical practice.

(1) data elements have been developed to monitor the clinical management of patients admitted to hospital with an acute coronary syndrome; (2) these data elements have been incorporated into the National health data dictionary; (3) the data elements are consistent with the international definition and are applicable to all patients admitted to hospital for an acute coronary syndrome.
the National Health Data Committee has endorsed a standard set of data elements for the management of patients with ACS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the quality and efficiency of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome.
improving the care of patients with acute myocardial infarction and acute coronary syndroms by developing a national data collection system for clinical care and outcomes research.
the clinical management of patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome.

these definitions and data elements are a necessary first step in the development of national clinical registries for patients with acute coronary syndrome.
the use of these data sets would provide a comprehensive picture of the management of ACS patients and the outcomes of that treatment.

the use of standardised data elements in the management of acute coronary syndrome patients will improve clinical care and facilitate the development of quality indicators and performance measures for the management of acute myocardial infarction.

the National Data Elements are now in place and the next stage is to develop a national registry for acute coronary syndroms.

the use of a national set of data definitions and a common data model can facilitate collaboration and improve data quality.

the development of a standardised set of national data elements for the care of patients with acute myocardial infarction and unstable angina will assist in the development of quality‐of‐care initiatives, performance indicators and clinical registries.
